correctness.rationale: For each time n, independence of fresh Bernoulli dyadic coefficients gives g_n(s)=product_{j<r_n:d_j(s)=1}(1-2p_nj), periodic modulo 2^{r_n}, with exact residue average b_n=product(1-p_nj). Binomial residues mix uniformly with error q_n exp(-pi^2 h/(2q_n^2)) for q_n<=n^gamma, gamma<1/2. Splitting temporal covariances into gaps below n^theta and longer gaps (2gamma<theta<1) gives polynomial L2 decay; Borel-Cantelli on a sufficiently sparse polynomial subsequence and bounded interpolation give almost-sure Cesaro bracket convergence. Bounded predictable-sign martingale increments yield the quenched functional CLT; conditional fourth moments provide uniform integrability and necessity of the deterministic Cesaro b_n correlation. The bounds eps^{r_n}<=b_n<=(1-eps)^{r_n} give exactly the natural-density criterion. Independently checked 84 rational product/residue identities for up to five active bits and 12 input steps; finite verification does not establish the almost-sure claim.

originality.rationale: Collevecchio–Hamza–Shi–Williams (2022) gives an abstract bootstrap martingale normality criterion but does not derive the environment-specific logarithmic-sparse dyadic bracket. Hamza–Tournier (2026) Theorem 2 obtains quenched standard independence only under ellipticity for ALL indexed coefficients, whereas the submitted model makes all non-dyadic coefficients identically zero; its Corollary 9 obtains an annealed one-factor Markov result. The target adds a nonzero-correlation classification and a necessary-and-sufficient density test in a sparse family, not a special case of the inspected prior hypotheses. This is a best-of-knowledge conclusion with alias risks.
